summary: Twelve comment-endorsed developer tools, apps, media, storage systems, and wearables from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Missionary Bush Pilot
items.source_story_title: I can't stop thinking about Papua New Guinea
items.summary: A YouTube channel following Kodiak bush-plane deliveries across Papua New Guinea.
items.why_included: A former viewer strongly recommended its aviation videos.
items.evidence: The commenter called the channel's aviation videos golden.

evidence_sources.author: tthbalazs
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you're into aviation, the videos are golden

items.name: System One Models
items.source_story_title: Introducing System One Models and Jev
items.summary: Fast classification models answering structured questions over arbitrary text or JSON.
items.why_included: A commenter praised the idea's speed, low cost, and flexible inputs.
items.evidence: The commenter independently described System One as a very promising idea.

evidence_sources.author: maltalex
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is a very promising idea - a model that takes arbitrary text input (which can be a complex json), plus a set of questions (yes/no, multiple-choice, or score) and quickly (milliseconds) and cheaply ($0.042/MTok) answers those questions.

items.name: Chrome Labs Text Editor
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Capsule – Single-file web apps that save their data into SQLite
items.summary: A browser text editor demonstrating direct local-file access on desktop and mobile.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as a working File System Access API example.
items.evidence: The commenter said the editor works nicely on both desktop and mobile.

evidence_sources.author: mg
evidence_sources.excerpt: It works nicely on Desktop and Mobile.

items.name: Capsule
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Capsule – Single-file web apps that save their data into SQLite
items.summary: A format for single-file web apps that store their data inside SQLite.
items.why_included: A commenter endorsed the project and connected it to portable agent-built artifacts.
items.evidence: The commenter positively assessed Capsule before explaining the value of portable SQLite artifacts.

evidence_sources.author: nzoschke
evidence_sources.excerpt: Looks neat. Shuffling artifacts around is more important than ever with all the agentic web sites and apps we are making.

items.name: Modem Thing
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Hacking a $20 4G wireless hotspot into a texting device
items.summary: A $20 4G hotspot repurposed into a compact keyboard-equipped texting cyberdeck.
items.why_included: A commenter praised both its practicality and the reused Clicks keyboard.
items.evidence: The commenter called the project cool, practical, and cleverly designed.

evidence_sources.author: xx_ns
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is a really cool project! A mini cyberdeck that doesn't seem too impractical to use.

items.name: JuiceFS
items.source_story_title: Alternatives to MinIO for single-node local S3
items.summary: A distributed POSIX file system backed by object storage and shared metadata.
items.why_included: A commenter named it as their own storage choice while discussing MinIO alternatives.
items.evidence: The commenter reported first-hand use of JuiceFS, with a trust caveat.

items.name: Silo
items.source_story_title: Alternatives to MinIO for single-node local S3
items.summary: The maintained PGSTY fork of MinIO, now renamed Silo, for S3-compatible storage.
items.why_included: A user praised the fork as an instant local S3 simulator with no complaints.
items.evidence: The commenter chose the former pgsty/minio fork and found it great for end-to-end tests.

evidence_sources.author: cadamsdotcom
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is what I went with.

items.name: ForgeCAD
items.summary: An agent-friendly JavaScript CAD environment for generating printable 3D models.
items.why_included: A user cut a multi-week modeling task to a working prototype in one hour.
items.evidence: The commenter called ForgeCAD mind-blowing and described successful printed household parts.

evidence_sources.author: atonse
evidence_sources.excerpt: ForgeCAD [1] for me was the first mind-blowing application of this a few months ago, where I'm able to just have claude (or codex) write JS that creates 3D Models that I can then print in my 3D printer.

items.name: GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: OpenAI's agentic model for professional workflows including editable Blender scene creation.
items.why_included: A Blender user gave Astra a concise, positive first-hand endorsement.
items.evidence: The commenter reported using Astra to create Blender objects and called it great.

evidence_sources.author: throwitaway222
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using Astra to just create things in Blender. It's great.

items.name: Wayback Machine
items.source_story_title: An update on Wayback Machine access
items.summary: Internet Archive's service for browsing preserved snapshots of websites across time.
items.why_included: A small-site owner explicitly praised its value for personal projects.
items.evidence: The commenter called the archive incredibly valuable and said they loved its benefits.

evidence_sources.author: Kodiack
evidence_sources.excerpt: They provide an incredibly valuable service and I love the benefit that I get from them just for personal side projects.

items.name: Oura Ring
items.summary: A low-maintenance smart ring focused on sleep, recovery, activity, and health tracking.
items.why_included: A year-long user praised its convenience and useful sleep-score signal.
items.evidence: The commenter found Oura unusually unfussy and useful for improving sleep health.

evidence_sources.author: atldev
evidence_sources.excerpt: I like my Oura ring and find it one of the least fussy fitness trackers I've used.

items.name: Garmin Lily 2 Active
items.summary: A compact GPS smartwatch supporting sleep, activity, and locally synced health data.
items.why_included: A Linux user recommended it after building a private Bluetooth sync workflow.
items.evidence: The commenter praised its tracking, local-data options, and explicitly recommended the watch.

evidence_sources.author: SequoiaHope
evidence_sources.excerpt: It’s really nice and my data is reasonably private (Claude can see it though I could fix that). I recommend the watch!
